text.p: British engineering group Babcock International Group Plc said on Wednesday trading in the first quarter of the financial year had been "satisfactory".
Chairman John Parker told the annual general meeting "good progress" was being made implementing the strategies, announced in June, to deal with its underperforming businesses.
Babcock said last month it was looking to sell its process division and its U.S. Electric Arc Furnace dust recycling plant.
"Discussions are now under way with a major engineering group which is interested in acquiring our process division," Parker said in a statement.
He also said plans for the Caldwell plant in the U.S. were proceeding to schedule and operations would cease in August.
The group in June reported a pre-tax loss of 22.0 million stg after exceptional charges in the year to March 31, versus profit of 3.1 million the year before.
The charges related to the write-off and termination of the Caldwell plant of 27.3 million stg. Other exceptionals amounted to a gain of 1.7 million stg.
